catalog_quote: Hintze 1975 p.167: "There are two tonemes. One is essentially high and the other low." p.168: "A small amount of length and loudness are in evidence along with pitch. However, the semantic load is not carried by these two features, but rather by the much more prominent element of pitch level." pp.175-176: "Stress a. Syllabic intensity or emphasis is semantically insignificant. Therefore, it is unmarked, since its occurrence is predictable. b. Both light and heavy stress occur. ... c. Stress Behavior - Relatively heavy stress occurs only where there is high tone. - Relatively light stress occurs elsewhere. - Relative stress that is light/heavy occurs in every word. Two syllable words: Some stress is always on the first syllable. ... Three syllable words: Word-final single marked toneme words are stressed relatively lightly on the second syllable. ... All others are stressed relatively he…

audit.reasoning: The 'tonal' coding (two-toneme register system; stress non-contrastive and predictable from tone, heavy stress only on high-toned syllables, light positional stress otherwise) rests on Hintze 1975, a dedicated 41-page phonemic statement with an explicit Stress subsection, which is held as page images with scanned; every quoted sentence was found verbatim at the cited pages (167, 168, 175-176 = PDF 23, 24, 31-32). The two held secondary sources (Lang 1973 PL C-20 p.xvii; SIL OPD 2004) independently state two tonemes / phonemic tone and defer to Hintze. A search of Glottolog 5.1 (all Enga-titled entries), the ANU repository, CrossRef, archive.org and Wikipedia's references found no later phonology, prosody dissertation, JIPA illustration or instrumental study of Enga; the newly fetched sources Lang 1971 ANU thesis is silent on stress rules but consistent (tone contrastive; initial stress mark on both

sources.citation: Lang, Adrianne. 1971. Nouns and classificatory verbs in Enga (New Guinea): a semantic study. PhD thesis, Australian National University. 236 pp. hdl:1885/132946
sources.quote: No stress rule stated. p.19 n.6 gives the phoneme list and 'Tone is contrastive /pilyo/ /pilyó/ [ˈpilyo] [ˈpilyó] 'I strike' / 'I do (work)'' (both members of the tonal minimal pair transcribed with an initial stress mark, consistent with Hintze's 'Two syllable words: Some stress is always on the first syllable'). p.34 n.3: 'One continuing problem has been that of the tonal system: Laycock (nd), Hintze (1960 and nd b), and Nida (1968) have all worked on the problem which is further complicated by dialectical variation.'
sources.locator: p.19 note 6 (PDF p.30); p.34 note 3 (PDF p.45)
